about: A candidate playbook for ab-run (deck@variant) and runner/ab.py --data: the shipped playbook with a hook on its attack (docs/agents/add_finish.py; DESIGN.md section 34). Only the playbook object is read.

playbook.notes: Mutant Menace (The Wise Mothman, BUG counters and rad/mill). Written from 12 stock goldfish games (seeds 23001-23012): stock kills on turn 11.3, casts Mothman on own turn 4 to 11 (median 5), never cast Bloatfly Swarm, Raul, Feral Ghoul, Struggle for Project Purity, Guardian Project or Contaminated Drink, and under-cast its ramp (Cultivate 1 of 5, Talisman of Dominance 1 of 5) and the counter doublers (Winding Constrictor, Hardened Scales held with the mana up). Rule 1: ramp first. Rule 2: the commander as soon as it can be cast (each mill of a nonland card of ours then grows the team). Rule 3: the counter doublers next, before the creatures they multiply. Rule 4: the engines (Raul, Hancock, Guardian Project, Inexorable Tide, Marcus, Scorchbeast, Mirelurk Queen). Rule 5: tap Raul in the first main phase so every player mills one before combat (Mothman, Mirelurk and Scorchbeast trigger on our own nonland mills), library 30 or more. Rule 6: the rest of the creatures, dearest first, whatever Forge thinks of them (Bloatfly Swarm was never cast by stock). Rule 7: Vault 87 and Struggle for Project Purity with 45 cards or more in the library (both draw). Rule 8: Biomass Mutation (AI:RemoveDeck:All) before combat at X 6 or more with three attackers. Rule 9: Contaminated Drink at X 3 or more with a short hand and a deep library. Rule 10: Harmonize. Rules 11-12: Strength Bobblehead's counters and Contagion Clasp's proliferate as after-combat mana sinks. Triggers: Scorchbeast's tokens and Radroach's return always; Tato Farmer's two rad counters on us only while Mothman or Scorchbeast turns our own mills into counters or tokens, with 50 cards left and 20 life. Answers (Putrefy, Atomize, Casualties of War, Nuclear Fallout, Find // Finality, Alpha Deathclaw's monstrosity, Rampaging Yao Guai, Mutational Advantage) are left to Forge for a second pass. || Version 2 (answers, written from the 200 tables of bots of ab-run #27, seed 20261260: the candidate won 55, stock 46). At the seat's losses the biggest opposing board held 12.5 creatures on average against our 3.8 (131 of 145 losses: more than ours; 111: six or more), and the seat died within a turn cycle from 19 life; Nuclear Fallout was in hand at 37 losses and cast in none of 52 games (stock: 0 of 45; Forge never casts it), Find // Finality 0 of 41. New rules 1-3, above everything, first main phase: Nuclear Fallout at X 3 (each creature -6/-6) when the strongest opposing board has more power than ours and four or more creatures; Nuclear Fallout at X 2 (-4/-4, kills tokens, spares our creatures with counters) when one opponent has six or more creatures and more than we do; Find // Finality on the same terms (Finality; whether the split card's Find half is taken instead is Forge's ordering, checked at the local tables). Rule 7 (after ramp, commander, doublers): Casualties of War, Alpha Deathclaw, Atomize when an opponent has a creature; targets and modes are Forge's (Casualties is cast only when Forge's logic agrees; Deathclaw is a plain creature cast and its enters trigger is aimed by Forge). Stock cast Deathclaw in 41 of 48 games and Casualties in 32 of 37; the engine rules starved both (10 of 51, 17 of 30). Rule 8: Vault 87 out of the old rule 7, with library 30 (was 45) and an opposing creature (chapter I steals a non-Mutant creature; chapter III draws by the greatest Mutant power). Rule 11: The Master's tap after Raul's mill in the first main phase (Forge aims it at a creature card milled this turn). Rule 12: Rampaging Yao Guai at X max, at least 3 (its artifact/enchantment destruction is Forge's choice). Rule 13 (the old rule 6) now names every creature and permanent the base left to Forge, which the play rules starved of mana: Lumbering Megasloth first (castable only when its counter discount makes it cheap), Nightkin Ambusher, The Master, Harold and Bob, Fraying Sanity, Power Fist. Stock cast them in 82 to 98% of the games drawn; the base in 17 to 60%. Rule 14: Struggle for Project Purity alone with library 45, as before. Rule 16: Mutational Advantage before combat with four attackers and three opposing creatures (our creatures with counters cannot be killed in that combat; then proliferate): the format cannot hold it for a wipe on another player's turn, and in hand it was cast in 1 of 38 games and held at 28 losses. Alpha Deathclaw's monstrosity is left to Forge: an activate rule cannot tell that the creature is already monstrous and would pay seven mana a turn for nothing. Local check, 8 tables of bots (seed 20263120): Nuclear Fallout cast by rule 1 twice (10 opposing permanents and none of ours left the battlefield; 8 opposing and 1 of ours); Finality cast once by rule 3 and countered (Swan Song); Find cast once by Forge's own choice; Alpha Deathclaw's enters trigger destroyed Doomwake Giant; Casualties took a creature, an enchantment and a land. Atomize was drawn once, in a game short of green, and is unverified: stock Forge cast it in 0 of 38 games, so Forge's logic may decline it under rule 7 too. Rule 16 (Mutational Advantage) never had four attackers. Shipped as version 2 on 2026-11-14 from ab-run #36: at 200 tables of bots (seed 20261310, opponents drawn from bots-v2 under their playbooks of 2026-11-13) 68 wins against its stock pilot's 51 (+8.5 points, 95% +1 to +16, exact test 0.050) with the attack left to Forge, the better of the two attacks on these tables (the same rules won 55 with the go-wide attack). What it casts in a share of games 15 points or more below its stock pilot on the same tables, 10 cards: Vault 12: The Necropolis (22 of 53 games drawn against 40 of 49), Agent Frank Horrigan (21 of 43 games drawn against 34 of 40), Fraying Sanity (28 of 40 games drawn against 36 of 37), Lumbering Megasloth (22 of 31 games drawn against 32 of 34), Harmonize (7 of 33 games drawn against 15 of 36), Nuka-Nuke Launcher (29 of 36 games drawn against 35 of 35), Tato Farmer (24 of 41 games drawn against 27 of 35), Strong, the Brutish Thespian (25 of 42 games drawn against 27 of 35) and 2 more. It casts 14 cards that much more often (demo-data/playtest/2026-11-14/second-pass/mutant-menace-forgeattack-card-diff.txt). VERSION 3 (2026-11-15). Version 3 = version 2 with Atomize taken out of the rule it shared with Casualties of War and Alpha Deathclaw (which left its aiming to Forge, and Forge never cast it: 0 of the 36 games it was drawn at the owner's table in ab-run #42, in hand at 23 losses; 0 of 42 under the stock pilot) and given a rule of its own right after: aimed at an opponent's nonland permanent worth four or more, the best one of the opponent that looks most dangerous (harness 0.3.4: aim). Nothing else is changed. Shipped as version 3 on 2026-11-15 from ab-run #43 (seed 20261360, the owner's table, opponents under their shipped playbooks): 43 wins of 200 against version 2's 42 on the same tables (+0.5 points, 95% -2 to +3, exact test 1.0); Atomize cast in 26 of the 30 games it was drawn (0 of 30 under version 2); its 26 casts went at the opponent that looked most dangerous 24 times and at the next one that had something worth four twice; 6 of them hit a commander and none fizzled. The rule it was read by was fixed before the run: level with or ahead of the shipped arm, and the newly named card cast in a quarter or more of the games it is drawn. VERSION 4 CANDIDATE `open` (2026-11-21). Version 3 with one change: after Forge's own attack has been declared, the creatures that stayed home attack an opponent that has no creature that can block, the most dangerous such opponent first: those that deal damage, have no ability that taps them (or have vigilance) and are not wanted home by Forge's own judgement of the seat's defence (`"open": true`; a weaker opponent is not killed this way while a more dangerous one lives). No cast or trigger rule is changed.
